sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 3

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 3:1
items.html:
Twelve kinds of records: a record of drawing and a record of clothing
The first kind is the record that remains from the lights after their departure, which comes from the phases of clothing. And the second kind is the record that remains from the lights after their departure, which comes from the phase of drawing. The meaning is that you already know that the greatness of the level is measured by the measure of coarseness in the screen, for the coarser it is, the greater the level it draws. It is also known that there are always two extremes to be discerned in this, set one against the other, for the greater the level, the farther apart those extremes are found, since just as the great level requires a coarser screen and a coarser vessel of Malchut, so it requires the more refined vessels of reception. For example, phase four, which is the coarsest and draws to herself the level of Keter, at the same time requires the most refined vessel, one fit to receive within her the light of Keter, as written of this in the Inner Observation in Part 2.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 3:2
items.html:
Records of drawing remain in the vessels of drawing, and those of clothing remain in the vessels of reception
Therefore it follows for us to discern, after every departure, two kinds of records: the first is the one that remains in the vessel of drawing of that light, and the second is the record that remains in the vessel of reception of that light. And in truth, if we judge by the record itself, they are almost one; indeed, by their origin they are as far from one another as the east is far from the west, for the record of the phase of drawing comes from the coarseness below which there is none, and the record of the phase of reception comes from a refinement above which there is none, for this one is phase four and that one is the phase of root.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 3:3
items.html:
The record of clothing is male and the record of coarseness is female
And know that they are discerned one relative to the other in the relation of male and female. This is because both of them are in truth one level of light, that is, a light clothed in the vessel properly fitted to it. But after the light departed from there, and the coarseness in the vessel became recognized as lowliness (as in the words of the ARI here, in Item 18), this great distance found between these two records was revealed before us. And since they are one from their beginning, they are therefore discerned as male and female.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 3:4
items.html:
The record of coarseness does not remain from the last phase after the refinement
And know that this record of the phase of female did not remain after the departure of the light from there. And although it is not lost, for there is no absence in spirituality, indeed it remains quiescent, without any action, until the end of correction. And this is what the ARI writes, that the last phase does not leave a record (Chapter 2, Item 6), and there remains there only the record of the phase of male alone. And this is what the ARI writes (in Chapter 2, Item 4): that when Keter rose and departed, it left one record in its place, in that vessel of its own, in order to illuminate from it to Hochma, which is beneath it, after it rises and departs. See there, and see there in the Inner Light.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 3:5
items.html:
Records that clothe in their own vessels
The third kind is the records that clothe in the place of the totality of the light that departed, that is, in the reflected light and the vessel of Malchut, which expanded of herself and within herself into ten Sefirot, for these clothed the ten Sefirot of direct light, as is known. Now the records that remain after their departure were likewise clothed, each and every one of them in them, according to its phase and according to its portion. For example, the Keter of direct light, which was clothed in the Nefesh of reflected light at the time of the expansion — afterwards, when it departed from there, the record is found clothing in its place, that is, in the Nefesh of reflected light. And likewise the record of Hochma in the Ruach of reflected light, etc. But certainly they did not require the whole measure of the vessel, for the record is a small part of the departing light; rather it took hold of a certain measure of the vessel, according to its portion. And this is brought in the words of the ARI here, Item 18. See there.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 3:6
items.html:
Records that do not clothe in their own vessels but stand above their own vessels
The fourth kind is the records that do not clothe in their own vessels, but each and every one of them is found above the vessel belonging to it, in the secret of the Tagin [crownlets] upon the letters, as brought in the words of the ARI here (Chapter 4, Item 4). And the reason for their going out from their own vessels is that, by force of the striking of the descending reflected light and the record upon one another — since the reflected light comes from the illumination of a coupling, it overpowered the record, which is of the phase of the remnants of the departure of the coupling; and since the light of the record is in oppositeness to the reflected light that descends into its vessel, they therefore cannot be together in one subject, that is, in one vessel. Therefore the record was compelled to depart from its vessel and to go out above its own vessel.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 3:7
items.html:
Records that returned to their own vessels
The fifth kind is the records that returned to their own vessels after they had gone out from there. For after the coupling departed from the upper phase as well, the illumination of the descending reflected light thereby departed too, and the sparks falling to the vessel beneath it were extinguished; and then the record returned into its vessel as before. For now it no longer has any opposition from the reflected light inside its vessel, since that too is after the departure of its own coupling; and therefore the record once again overpowers the reflected light. And the reason that the departure of that coupling is called the extinguishing of the sparks is that the illumination of reflected light is called by the name sparks, and therefore the cessation of its illumination is called by the name extinguishing, which is the term customary with sparks of fire. Understand this.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 3:8
items.html:
A record comprising refined light and coarse light; a record from refined light; a record from coarse light
The sixth kind is a record that comprises refined light and coarse light. The seventh kind is what is called the refined light, brought here in the words of the ARI (Chapter 2, Item 10). The eighth kind is what is called the coarse light of the record, brought in Etz Chaim (Gate of Mati ve-Lo Mati [reaching and not reaching], Chapter 3).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 3:9
items.html:
Just as in the lights of the first expansion the refined light was mixed with the coarse light, so it is in the record left by the first expansion
The explanation of the matter is that whatever there is in the light there is likewise in the record that remains from that light. Therefore the record is called by the name the impression of a seal, as written (in the Inner Light, Chapter 2, Item 3). And therefore the records that remain from the lights of the first expansion comprise light and vessel, similar to the lights from which they came, as above in Item 44. See there. But so long as the record is clothed in its vessel, there is no recognition there between light and vessel, similar to the lights of the first expansion, in which the lights and the vessels are mixed, as brought here (in the words of the ARI, Chapter 6, Item 2, and see there in the Inner Light, Item 6). And therefore in the record that comes from them too, nothing is recognized between the light and the vessel; rather they are mixed together. And this is the sixth kind mentioned above, that is, the record comprising refined light and coarse light, but the coarse light is not recognized in it; rather it is mixed within it, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 3:10
items.html:
After the departure of the record from the vessel, the coarseness in the vessel was revealed
Now you will understand the seventh and eighth kinds mentioned above. For it was explained above in Item 45, in the matter of the fourth kind of record, that because of the striking of the descending reflected light upon the record, the record departed and went out from its vessel and rose above it from above, in the secret of the Tagin [crownlets] upon the letters. See there. And now, because of the departure of the record from the vessel, the difference between the vessel and the record was revealed, for now the coarseness in the vessel is recognized, which is now discerned by the name coarse light, similar to the lights of the first expansion (in Chapter 6, and in the Inner Light there, Item 7). See there. And you already know that whatever applies in the lights applies likewise in the records that come from them.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 3:11
items.html: Now it has been explained that after the departure of the record from the vessel, a difference was revealed between the light of the record and the vessel of the record, and the vessel is now called the coarse light of the record. And know that from the coarse light in the record the vessels of the males of the second expansion were made. And the light of the record is now called the refined light in the record, and from it the lights of the males of the second expansion were made, as the ARI writes (in the Gate of Mati ve-Lo Mati, Chapter 3 — see there well). And remember this.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 3:12
items.html:
The record of clothing that remains in Malchut
The ninth kind is the record of the light of Malchut, brought in the words of the ARI here (Chapter 6, Item 20). And know that this record is of the seventh kind mentioned above, which is called refined light, that is, that there is no phase of vessel in it, as written above in Item 43, that the record of the phase of drawing was lost — and that is the phase of the coarse light of this record, which is the eighth kind of record. But the refined light in it remained without a vessel, and it therefore rose above its own vessel, that is, to Yesod. (Chapter 4, Items 2 and 3)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 3:13
items.html:
The records included in the screen after it was refined
The tenth kind is the records that were included in the screen on its way up to the Emanator. For the light of Malchut, which is the screen and the reflected light in her, is refined and rises from phase to phase until it comes to the Emanator, that is, to the Peh [mouth] of the Rosh [head]; and as it passes through them, it is also included from the records that the lights left there after their departure. Therefore, when it came to the Peh, it was comprised of all three phases of records, upon which the coupling was made anew, so that from there emerged the vessels and the lights of the second expansion, as written of this at length (in the Inner Light, Chapter 4, Item 4).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 3:14
items.html:
The records that remained from the four levels that emerged at the time of the refinement
The eleventh kind is the records that remained from the four levels that emerge at the time of the refinement, from the phase of the first nine Sefirot in them. For the ARI speaks here only of the records that remained from the first nine of the first expansion, before it began to be refined, which is called the first light, as the ARI writes here (Chapter 3, Item 8). Indeed, the four levels that emerged afterwards, at the time of the refinement, also left records in their vessels after they departed, namely likewise from the first nine Sefirot in them, for the last phase does not leave a record, as is known.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 3:15
items.html:
The records of clothing that remained from the last phases in the four levels mentioned above
The twelfth kind is the records that remained from the last phases in the four levels mentioned above, which emerged at the time of the refinement — and that is only the phase of the refined light in those records, for the coarse light in those records was lost from the last phases, as was explained with regard to the last phases of the records that remained from the first light (above in Items 29 and 51. See there).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 3:16
items.html: Now the twelve kinds of records have been explained, which are: 1. the records that come from the phase of clothing, explained in Items 40, 42, 43 and 41. 2. the records that come from the phase of drawing, explained likewise in those same items. 3. the records that clothe within their own vessels, explained in Item 44. 4. the records that do not clothe in their own vessels, but are in the secret of the Tagin [crownlets] upon the letters, explained in Item 44. 5. the records that returned to their own vessels after they had gone out from there, explained in Item 46. 6. the records comprising refined light and coarse light, in which the coarse light is not recognized, explained in Items 47, 48 and 49. 7. the refined light of the records, from which the lights of the males of the second expansion were made, explained likewise in the items mentioned above. 8. the coarse light of the records, from which vessels were made for the males of the second expansion, explained likewise (ibid.), and in Item 50. 9. the record of the light of Malchut, which is only of the phase of the refined light in this record, for the last phase does not leave a record, explained in Item 51. 10. the records that were included in the screen on its way up to the Emanator, where they were renewed in a coupling for the second expansion, explained in Item 52. 11. the records that remained from the first nine Sefirot of the four levels that emerged at the time of the refinement, explained in Item 52. 12. the records of the last phases from those levels, explained in Item 54.
